original_question: A numerical semigroup Gamma is called cyclotomic if the polynomial P_Gamma(z) determined by the Hilbert series H_Gamma(z) = P_Gamma(z)/(1-z) is a product of cyclotomic polynomials. Is a numerical semigroup a complete intersection if and only if it is cyclotomic?
target_in_paper: Section 7 (Complete intersections), Problem 27 of arXiv:2406.00790, which restates the Ciolan–García-Sánchez–Moree conjecture that a numerical semigroup is a complete intersection if and only if it is cyclotomic.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem and its core mathematical content: it uses the Hilbert-series/semigroup-polynomial definition of cyclotomicity and asks exactly whether cyclotomic numerical semigroups coincide with complete intersection numerical semigroups. This matches the official formulation recorded in the paper.
missing_details: The paper works with a numerical semigroup S as a cofinite additive submonoid of N; this should be stated explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
The Hilbert series should be written explicitly as H_{k[S]}(z)=sum_{s in S} z^s, i.e. the Hilbert series of the semigroup ring k[S]=k[t^s : s in S] with its natural grading deg(t^s)=s.
The polynomial should be defined explicitly as P_S(z)=(1-z)H_{k[S]}(z), so that P_S(z) lies in Z[z]; the factorization is meant in Z[z] as a product of cyclotomic polynomials.

The meaning of 'complete intersection numerical semigroup' is implicit in the draft but explicit in the paper: it means nu(S)=e(S)-1, equivalently that k[S] (and equivalently the local semigroup ring) is a complete intersection.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the conjecture is about all numerical semigroups, with no extra restrictions on embedding dimension, multiplicity, or characteristic.

The paper notes that the forward implication complete intersection => cyclotomic is already known/easy, so the genuinely open content is the converse cyclotomic => complete intersection; this is worth recording as an equivalent reformulation.
refined_question: Let S be a numerical semigroup, i.e. a cofinite additive submonoid of N, and let k[S]=k[t^s : s in S] be its semigroup ring over a field k, graded by deg(t^s)=s. Write its Hilbert series as H_{k[S]}(z)=sum_{s in S} z^s=P_S(z)/(1-z), where P_S(z)=(1-z)sum_{s in S} z^s in Z[z]. Call S cyclotomic if P_S(z) factors in Z[z] as a product of cyclotomic polynomials. Must every cyclotomic numerical semigroup be a complete intersection numerical semigroup (equivalently, does nu(S)=e(S)-1, or equivalently is k[S] a complete intersection), so that S is a complete intersection if and only if it is cyclotomic?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since every complete intersection numerical semigroup is cyclotomic, is every cyclotomic numerical semigroup a complete intersection numerical semigroup?
justification: The draft is aiming at the complete-intersection/cyclotomic conjecture recorded in the survey as Problem 27 in Section 7. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the rewrite adds the paper's ambient semigroup-ring setup, the explicit Hilbert-series formula, the semigroup polynomial P_S, and the paper's meaning of 'complete intersection numerical semigroup'. I did not narrow the question to the verified two-irreducible-factor case from the cited paper with Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.3, because arXiv:2406.00790 records the broader open problem. Also, arXiv:2406.00790 itself is a survey and does not contain labels Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 under those numbers; the nearest official formulation inside this paper is Problem 27, while the cited literature supplies the equivalent one-sided reformulation and the known special case.
